# minisql — Read-only SQL Engine over CSV Files — Specification

**Status:** Not Started
**Dependencies:** none (greenfield repository; seed commit `6886f6e`)
**Layer:** Domain (self-contained library + CLI)
**Priority:** Critical Path
**Estimated Complexity:** ~10 tasks across 4 implementation phases
**Authority:** `contract.md` at the repository root is authoritative. This specification restates, organises and disambiguates it; where this document and `contract.md` differ, `contract.md` wins. Nothing here removes or weakens a contract requirement.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Build `minisql`, a Python standard-library-only query engine that executes a read-only SQL subset over a directory of CSV files. Each `.csv` file is a table whose column types (INTEGER / REAL / TEXT) are inferred from the data. The engine is a real pipeline — tokenizer → recursive-descent parser producing an AST → semantic analyzer (name resolution, static typing, aggregate validation, table IO) → staged executor — exposed as a library API (`minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`), a one-shot CLI (`python -m minisql`) printing CSV or an aligned table, and an interactive REPL. Errors are always a single line naming the kind and exact query line/column; never a traceback. Output is byte-for-byte deterministic on Windows, macOS and Linux. Pytest tests accompany the implementation.

## 2. Problem Statement

### Current State
The repository contains only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore` (`__pycache__/`). There is no code, no tests, no prior spec (Codebase Analyst, repo scan).

### Impact of Inaction
The contract (R1–R21, AC1–AC12) is unmet; hidden tests (AC12) reproduce contract behaviour byte-for-byte, so every deviation in output text, error position or exit code is a failure.

## 3. Goals & Non-Goals

### Goals
- G1. Satisfy every functional requirement R1–R21 and acceptance criterion AC1–AC12 of `contract.md` exactly.
- G2. Engine structure: separate tokenizer, parser/AST, semantic analysis, executor modules.
- G3. Library API, one-shot CLI and REPL per contract interface rules.
- G4. Exact error classes, messages and positions; no traceback on any path.
- G5. Deterministic byte output on all three OSes (UTF-8, `\n`).
- G6. A pytest suite covering each requirement, all ACs verbatim, and the edge cases in §5.
- G7. Code runs on Python ≥ 3.11 (contract) and, for local verification in this environment, also on Python 3.9 (see D1).

### Non-Goals
- Writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL), subqueries, UNION, CASE, BETWEEN, scalar functions other than the five aggregates, RIGHT/FULL/CROSS joins, `COUNT(DISTINCT …)`, multiple statements per query.
- Indexes, query optimisation, caching of table data between `execute` calls (files are re-read on each `execute`).
- Any third-party runtime dependency; `sqlite3` or any SQL engine/parser (forbidden by R1).

## 4. Architecture

```
SQL text ─► lexer.tokenize ─► sqlparser.parse ─► analyzer.analyze(query, catalog) ─► executor.run(plan) ─► Result
                                                     │  (loads referenced CSVs, FROM order)
DIR ─► catalog.Catalog (scan dir, resolve stems, read/infer CSV)                    formatting.format_csv / format_table
api.connect / Connection ── cli.main (one-shot | repl.run)
```

### Module layout (flat package `minisql/` at repo root)

Names avoid stdlib clashes (`ast`, `parser`, `csv`, `token`, `types`, `io`) (Codebase Analyst §2).

| Module | Responsibility | Contract ownership |
|---|---|---|
| `minisql/errors.py` | `MiniSQLError` + `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`; `kind`, `line`, `column`, `message`; `__str__`; offset→(line, col) helper | R21 (format) |
| `minisql/lexer.py` | Token stream with kind, value, source text, start/end offsets | R4, R6 (keywords), Lex errors |
| `minisql/nodes.py` | AST dataclasses with source spans and error-position offsets; `Paren` node | R5, R10, R14 support |
| `minisql/sqlparser.py` | Recursive-descent parser per EBNF and precedence | R5, Parse errors |
| `minisql/catalog.py` | Directory scan, stem resolution, CSV reading, header checks, type inference | R2, R3, IO errors |
| `minisql/analyzer.py` | Name resolution/scopes, static types, `*` expansion, output names, aggregate-query detection and grouping validation, ORDER BY resolution, DISTINCT check, ESCAPE check; produces a bound plan | R6, R7, R10, R12 (checks), R14 (resolution), Semantic errors |
| `minisql/evaluate.py` | Runtime value operations: arithmetic (truncating `/`, sign-of-dividend `%`, `fmod`), NULL propagation, division by zero, 3VL, IN, comparisons → `int`, LIKE matcher | R8, R9, Runtime errors |
| `minisql/executor.py` | Staged execution of the 9 evaluation steps | R11–R16 |
| `minisql/formatting.py` | Value text, `format_csv`, `format_table` | R18 |
| `minisql/api.py` | `connect`, `Connection`, `Result` | R17 |
| `minisql/cli.py` | argparse, stream setup, one-shot mode, exit codes, no-traceback guard | R19 |
| `minisql/repl.py` | Prompt, buffering, dot-commands, EOF | R20 |
| `minisql/__init__.py` | Re-exports public API and error classes | R1, R17 |
| `minisql/__main__.py` | `sys.exit(cli.main())` | R1 |

Tests live in `tests/` (pytest), with a repo-root `conftest.py` so `import minisql` works under plain `pytest` (Codebase Analyst §1.5).

## 5. Detailed Design

Each subsection restates the governing contract rule and adds the binding design decisions. Decision IDs (Dn) are collected in §5.12.

### 5.1 Errors and positions (R21)
- `MiniSQLError(Exception)` with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`. `str(err)` = `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO: `IOError: <message>`. Kind `Runtime` prints `RuntimeError at …` (class name `QueryRuntimeError`).
- All positions derive from an absolute code-point offset into the SQL text via one helper: `line = sql.count('\n', 0, off) + 1`; `column = off - (sql.rfind('\n', 0, off) + 1) + 1`. Lines split on `\n` only; tab and `\r` count as one column (Domain Expert F1).
- Message templates and positions exactly per the contract table (Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime/IO). `N`, `R`, `F` as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`); `OP` as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates.
- Phase order: lex the whole input → parse fully → semantic (including IO for referenced tables in FROM order) → execute. All static errors are raised before any row is evaluated.

### 5.2 Lexer (R4, R6)
- Whitespace exactly space, tab, `\r`, `\n`; anything else outside a token (e.g. NBSP, form feed, `#`, lone `!`) → `unexpected character 'X'` at that character.
- `--` comment to end of line (so `SELECT --1` is followed by EOF).
- Character classes are ASCII-only: identifiers `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; digits `[0-9]`. Never `str.isdigit/isalpha/isidentifier` or `\d` (Integration F25–26, Domain Expert F1).
- Keywords (case-insensitive, reserved): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`. Function names are identifiers.
- Quoted identifier `"..."` (`""` → `"`), may contain anything incl. newlines, may equal a keyword; unterminated → `unterminated quoted identifier` at the opening quote.
- String `'...'` (`''` → `'`), may span lines, backslash literal; unterminated → `unterminated string literal` at opening quote.
- Numbers: INTEGER `[0-9]+`; REAL `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. Longest match of these forms; if the next character is an ASCII letter, digit, `_` or `.` → `invalid number literal` at the literal start. Thus `12abc`, `1e`, `1e+`, `1..2`, `1.2.3`, `1_0`, `1.5e` are errors; `1.`, `1.e5`, `.5` are valid; `.` not followed by a digit is the `.` operator. REAL value = `float(text)`, INTEGER value = `int(text)`.
- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . ;` and `*`.
- Each token carries `kind`, `value`, `text = sql[start:end]`, `start`, `end`. An EOF token sits at offset `len(sql)` ("one past last input character").

### 5.3 Parser (R5)
- Recursive descent over the contract EBNF. Level 4 (comparison / IS / LIKE / IN) is non-associative: `cmp` parses at most one tail; a second comparison operator surfaces as `unexpected token '<text>'` at that operator (`a = b = c`, `a IS NULL IS NULL`).
- `NOT` binds looser than comparison (`NOT 1 = 2` = `NOT (1 = 2)` → 1); `1 = NOT 2` → ParseError at `NOT`.
- `unexpected token 'T'` uses the token's exact source text (strings keep their quotes, keywords keep written case). At EOF: `unexpected end of input` at offset `len(sql)`.
- Calls: `name "(" ("*" | expr) ")"`; whitespace allowed between name and `(`; quoted names may be calls. `COUNT()`, `COUNT(DISTINCT x)`, `f(a, b)`, `COUNT(t.*)` → ParseErrors at the offending token.
- `item`: `*` | `name . *` (3-token lookahead) | `expr [[AS] name]`; an alias without `AS` is any IDENT/QUOTED_IDENT token.
- `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take an INTEGER literal token only (`LIMIT -1`, `LIMIT 1.5` are ParseErrors); `OFFSET` without `LIMIT` is legal; `OFFSET … LIMIT …` is a ParseError at `LIMIT`. Optional single `;` then EOF.
- AST nodes record `start`/`end` (first to last character of the construct), a `pos` offset for error reporting (operator token for binary/unary/logical/comparison ops; the `LIKE`/`IN` keyword for `[NOT] LIKE`/`[NOT] IN` (D9); function-name token for calls; first token for column refs; the `*` token in calls; the ESCAPE string token), and a distinct `Paren(expr)` node whose span includes the parentheses (Domain Expert F1).

### 5.4 Data directory and CSV loading (R2, R3)
- `connect(DIR)`: if `DIR` is missing or not a directory → `DataIOError("data directory not found: DIR")` immediately (DIR as given, `str(os.fspath(DIR))`).
- Table discovery: fresh `os.scandir` on every `execute`/`tables()`; a table is an entry with `entry.is_file()` (follows symlinks; excludes directories, FIFOs, broken links) whose name ends with `.csv` case-insensitively; stem = `name[:-4]` (D12). Lookup is case-insensitive (`str.lower()`); two stems equal case-insensitively → `ambiguous table file '<name>'` (name as written in the query) for any reference.
- Read with `open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='')` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)`, streaming as the contract literally states (D5). Only tables referenced in FROM/JOIN are read, in FROM order, during semantic analysis.
- Records with zero fields (blank lines, before or after the header) are skipped. The first non-empty record is the header; no header → `<file>: empty file` (empty file, BOM-only, blank-lines-only).
- Header: names used verbatim; empty name → `<file>: empty column name`; duplicate names (case-insensitive) → `<file>: duplicate column 'C'` with `C` the second occurrence as written.
- Field-count mismatch → `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M` with N = `reader.line_num` after that record. `csv.Error` → `<file>: line N: malformed CSV` with N = `line_num` when raised. `UnicodeDecodeError` → `<file>: invalid UTF-8`. Other `OSError` while opening/reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` (D13; no contract template, defensive only).
- `<file>` is the base file name as on disk.
- Type inference per column over non-empty raw fields (no trimming) using `re.fullmatch` with explicit ASCII classes: all match `[+-]?[0-9]+` → INTEGER (`int`); else all match `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` → REAL (`float`); else TEXT (verbatim). No non-empty fields → TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. `re.fullmatch` is required (`re.match(...$)` would accept a trailing `\n`) (Codebase Analyst §3.35).
- `tables()` lists stems sorted by `(s.lower(), s)` without reading contents; ambiguous stems are both listed (D14). `schema(table)` loads the table (with IO errors as above) and returns `[(column, type)]` in header order; unknown table → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 (D15).

### 5.5 Name resolution and output names (R6, R10)
- Range name of a tableref = alias if present, else table name; a table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier (`emp.id` with `FROM emp e` → `unknown column 'emp.id'`). Duplicate range names (case-insensitive) → `duplicate table name 'N'` at the second tableref's range-name token.
- Unqualified `c` searches all FROM tables; `q.c` searches range `q`; zero matches → `unknown column 'R'`, more than one → `ambiguous column 'R'`, at the column-ref start. ON sees only tables introduced before or in its own join. Joins associate left. All name matching is case-insensitive.
- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in FROM order; `t.*` to that table's columns; unknown/hidden `t` → `unknown table 't'` at the `t` token (D10). `SELECT *` without FROM expands to zero columns (D11).
- Output name: alias as written (quotes removed, `""` → `"`); else for an unparenthesized column reference (qualified or not), the column's header name from the CSV; else verbatim source text `sql[item.start:item.end]` (keeps inner whitespace/comments/newlines; e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).

### 5.6 Static typing (R7)
- Types: INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, NULL (bare `NULL` literal only, plus results derived per rules below). LEFT JOIN does not change a column's static type (D2).
- Arithmetic `+ - * / %`: operands INTEGER/REAL/NULL else `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2` at the operator. Result REAL if either REAL; else NULL if both NULL; else INTEGER. Unary `-`/`+`: operand numeric/NULL else `cannot apply 'OP' to T`; result keeps operand type.
- Comparisons and each `IN` item vs `x`: both numeric, both TEXT, or either NULL; else two-type mismatch (OP as written; `IN` for IN). Result INTEGER.
- `LIKE`: both operands TEXT or NULL, else `cannot apply 'LIKE' to T1 and T2` at the `LIKE` token; `ESCAPE` string must be exactly one code point else `ESCAPE must be a single character` at the ESCAPE string. Result INTEGER.
- `IS [NOT] NULL`: any operand; INTEGER.
- `AND`/`OR`: operands numeric/NULL else two-type mismatch (`AND`/`OR`); `NOT`: single-type mismatch (`NOT`). Results INTEGER.
- `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` condition of type TEXT → `condition must be numeric, got TEXT` at the condition expression's start (first character, e.g. `(` for `WHERE (name)`). Checks run bottom-up, so inner operator mismatches are reported first.
- Aggregates: `COUNT(*)`/`COUNT(e)` → INTEGER (any type). `SUM`: INTEGER→INTEGER, REAL→REAL, NULL→NULL (D4), TEXT → `cannot apply 'SUM' to TEXT` at the function name. `AVG`: numeric/NULL → REAL, TEXT → `cannot apply 'AVG' to TEXT`. `MIN`/`MAX`: any type, keeps argument type. Non-COUNT `X(*)` → `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT` at the `*`. Unknown name → `unknown function 'F'` at the name (checked before the `*` rule, D16).
- Result `types` list uses `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"`, `"NULL"`.

### 5.7 Aggregation (R12)
- Aggregate query iff `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or ORDER BY.
- Structural identity via canonical keys after resolution: `Paren` transparent; column → `('col', table_idx, col_idx)`; literal → `('lit', TYPE, value)` (type tag so `1` ≠ `1.0`); operators by canonical op (`<>` ≡ `!=`, D8) and child keys; aggregates by upper-case name and `'*'`/argument key (Domain Expert F2).
- Validation (select, HAVING, ORDER BY): a node whose key matches a GROUP BY key is OK; an aggregate is OK (argument must contain no aggregate); a literal is OK; a bare column ref otherwise → `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate` at the column ref; else recurse. `*`/`t.*` → `'*' not allowed in aggregate query` at the `*`. Aggregates in WHERE, ON, GROUP BY or inside another aggregate → `aggregate function not allowed here` at that function name.
- GROUP BY has no ordinals or alias references (`GROUP BY 1` groups by the constant; HAVING cannot see aliases).
- Without GROUP BY: one group over the whole filtered input, even when empty; without HAVING exactly one row; HAVING filters to 0 or 1 row. With GROUP BY: empty input → zero rows; groups in first-seen order (dict keyed by tuple of key values; NULL equals NULL).
- `COUNT(*)` counts rows (including LEFT JOIN NULL-filled rows); `COUNT(e)` non-NULL values; all others ignore NULLs; over zero non-NULL values COUNT is 0, others NULL. SUM accumulates left-to-right with `+` (never `sum()`/`math.fsum`, whose float results differ across versions — Integration F23). AVG = sum/count with true division (exact int sum for INTEGER). MIN/MAX replace only on strict `<`/`>` (first seen kept on ties).

### 5.8 Execution and evaluation order (R8, R9, R11, R13–R16)
Staged full passes, exactly per contract:
1. FROM/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; every matching pair emitted; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled right side after all pairs for an unmatched left row. No FROM → exactly one empty row.
2. WHERE per row. 3. Group keys then aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. HAVING per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. ORDER BY keys. 7. DISTINCT (first occurrence kept; NULL equals NULL). 8. Stable sort. 9. OFFSET, then LIMIT.
- Consequences: `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp LIMIT 0` raises; `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp WHERE 0` does not; select errors are reported before ORDER BY key errors; no constant folding.
- Evaluator compiled to closures over flat joined-row tuples; column identity `(table_idx, col_idx)` maps to a flat index.
- `AND`: evaluate left; if false → 0 without right; else evaluate right; false → 0; else NULL if either NULL; else 1. `OR` mirror. NULL left still evaluates right. Truthiness: nonzero true, zero false (`0.0`, `-0.0` false), NULL unknown.
- Arithmetic: evaluate both operands left-to-right; NULL → NULL; zero divisor (INTEGER 0 or REAL ±0.0) for `/` or `%` → `division by zero` at the operator. INTEGER `/`: `q = abs(a)//abs(b)`, negated if signs differ; INTEGER `%`: `a - b*q` (sign of dividend). REAL (either operand REAL): `/` true division, `%` `math.fmod`, operands converted with `float()`. Never `int(a/b)` or Python `%` (Integration F21).
- Comparisons return `int` 1/0 (never `bool`), NULL if either operand NULL. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering; numerics compare numerically.
- `IN`: evaluate `x` then all items left-to-right (no short-circuit, D6); NULL if `x` NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item NULL; else 0; `NOT IN` negates with 3VL. `IS [NOT] NULL` → 1/0.
- `LIKE`: if any operand (value, pattern, escape) is NULL → NULL (checked first, D7). Otherwise compile the whole pattern: escape char `c` followed by `%`, `_`, or `c` → literal; followed by anything else or at end → `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. Match whole-string, case-sensitive, code-point-wise with a regex-free two-pointer wildcard matcher (`%` any sequence incl. empty, `_` exactly one code point incl. newline). `NOT LIKE` negates with 3VL. Never pre-validate at analysis time.
- ORDER BY resolution: bare INTEGER literal → 1-based ordinal after `*` expansion (`0` or > column count → `ORDER BY position N is out of range` at the ordinal, N = `str(int value)`); bare unqualified identifier equal (case-insensitive) to exactly one explicit select alias → that output column (two → `ambiguous column 'R'`); otherwise an expression over input rows (or groups). `-1`, `(1)` are expressions. With DISTINCT each item must be an ordinal, alias, or structurally identical to a select expression, else `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used` at the expression start; such items map to output-column values.
- Sort: successive stable `list.sort` passes from last key to first, key `(v is not None, v)`, `reverse=True` for DESC — NULL smallest (first ASC, last DESC); ties keep pre-sort order in both directions (Domain Expert F3).
- `LIMIT 0` → no rows; OFFSET past end → no rows.

### 5.9 Library API (R17)
```python
minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
Connection.tables() -> list[str]
Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
```
Exports: `connect`, `Connection`, `Result`, `format_csv`, `format_table`, `MiniSQLError`, `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`. Importing `minisql` must not alter `sys.stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None` (never `bool`).

### 5.10 Output formats (R18)
- Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
- CSV: header line, then one line per row; fields joined by `,`; every line ends `\n`. NULL → empty unquoted field. Quote a field (wrap in `"`, double inner `"`) iff it is the empty string, contains `,` `"` `\n` `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names use the same quoting. Hand-written (not `csv.writer`).
- Table: cell text = value text with `\n`→`\\n` and `\r`→`\\r` (two-character escapes), NULL → `NULL`; headers escaped the same way (D17). Width = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and NULL left-aligned (column alignment by the column's result type; NULL cells always left). Cells joined by ` | `; separator `-`×width joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; footer `(1 row)` or `(N rows)` (incl. `(0 rows)`); every line ends `\n`. A column of type NULL holds only NULL cells (left-aligned).

### 5.11 CLI and REPL (R19, R20)
- `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`; argparse with `allow_abbrev=False`, `--data` default `.`, `--format` `choices=['csv','table']` default `None` (one-shot → csv, REPL → table), positional `sql` `nargs='?'`; `args.sql is not None` → one-shot (so `""` is one-shot with empty SQL). Usage errors: argparse exit 2.
- Stream setup in `cli.main()` only (never at import): `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='backslashreplace', newline='\n')`; `sys.stdin` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', newline='\n')` (Integration F11–F15; D18).
- One-shot: `connect` first (missing DIR → `IOError: …` exit 3 before lexing); execute; format the full output string, then write once. Errors: stdout empty, stderr exactly `str(err) + "\n"`; exit 1 for Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime, 3 for IO, 0 on success.
- Top-level guard: catch `MiniSQLError`; catch `BrokenPipeError` (redirect stdout to devnull, exit 1); `KeyboardInterrupt` (exit 130); any other unexpected `Exception` (e.g. `OverflowError`, `RecursionError`) → a single line `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <exception text>` on stderr, exit 1 (D19) — never a traceback.
- REPL: prompt `minisql> ` when buffer empty, `   ...> ` (three spaces) otherwise, written to stdout without newline and flushed, regardless of TTY. Input not echoed. Read lines with `readline()`; strip one trailing `\n` only (keep `\r`; D18). With an empty buffer: a line whose stripped text (strip `' \t\r\n'`) starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise append the line (joined with `\n`); when the buffer right-stripped ends with `;`, execute it and clear the buffer.
- Commands (exact lower-case): `.help` (free text to stdout), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line; errors as one stderr line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit`, `.exit` (exit 0). Anything else (incl. `.format` with a bad/missing argument, `.schema` with no name) → stderr `unknown command: <stripped line>` (D20).
- Results print in the current format (CSV has no footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer. stdout is flushed before each stderr write.
- At EOF: a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. A missing `--data` DIR in REPL mode → `IOError: …` on stderr, exit 3 before the first prompt (D21).

### 5.12 Decision register

Decisions taken where `contract.md` is silent or researchers diverged. Each picks the option closest to the contract text; the alternative is recorded.

| ID | Decision | Alternative (rejected) | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Code targets Python ≥ 3.11 but must also run on 3.9 (no `match`, no runtime PEP 604 unions, no 3.10+ stdlib APIs, `from __future__ import annotations`). Local validation uses `python` 3.9.6. | Validate with 3.14 — the Domain Expert reported `/usr/local/bin/python3.14` available, but it is SIGKILLed on launch (exit 137, verified by orchestrator and Integration Researcher); not usable. | Environment evidence; contract requires ≥3.11 at runtime only |
| D2 | LEFT JOIN NULL-filled columns keep their inferred static type | Give them NULL type | "Any value may be None" |
| D3 | `types` entry `"NULL"` only for NULL-typed expressions (bare NULL, `-NULL`, `NULL+NULL`, `SUM/MIN/MAX(NULL)`); predicates over NULL are INTEGER | — | Contract type rules |
| D4 | `SUM(NULL)` → NULL type; `AVG(NULL)` → REAL; `MIN/MAX(NULL)` → NULL | Reject NULL-typed aggregate arguments | NULL type accepted wherever numeric is |
| D5 | CSV read by streaming `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` over the open file; first raised error wins | Decode whole file first so invalid UTF-8 always wins (Codebase Analyst A24) | Literal contract wording; oracle uses single-error files |
| D6 | `IN` does not short-circuit; `x` and all items evaluated left-to-right | Stop at first match | Only AND/OR are specified to short-circuit |
| D7 | LIKE: NULL operand checked before pattern validation → NULL | Validate pattern first | Mirrors "NULL … (checked first)" for arithmetic; "Any NULL operand gives NULL" |
| D8 | `<>` and `!=` structurally identical; literals identical by (type, value) | Textual identity | "same resolved columns, operators and literals" |
| D9 | `NOT LIKE`/`NOT IN` type errors use OP `LIKE`/`IN` at the `LIKE`/`IN` token | Position at `NOT` | Runtime LIKE errors are "at the `LIKE` token" |
| D10 | `q.*` with unknown/hidden `q` → `unknown table 'q'` at `q` | unknown column | Template list; table/name token |
| D11 | `SELECT *` without FROM → zero output columns, one row | SemanticError | Do not invent errors |
| D12 | Stem = `name[:-4]`; a file literally named `.csv` has stem `''` | `pathlib.Path.stem` | Contract "file stem" of `*.csv` |
| D13 | Non-decode OSError while reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` | Traceback | No-traceback rule; no template exists |
| D14 | `tables()` lists ambiguous stems (both) | Raise | "lists stems without reading file contents" |
| D15 | `schema(unknown)` → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 | DataIOError | Template exists only as Semantic |
| D16 | Unknown function reported before `'*'` argument rule | Reverse | Single-error oracle; name resolution precedes argument checks |
| D17 | Table format escapes `\n`/`\r` in header cells too | Escape only values | Preserves one-line rows |
| D18 | REPL stdin reconfigured to UTF-8 with `newline='\n'` (no CRLF translation; `\r` kept, lexer treats it as whitespace); stdin `errors='replace'` | Universal newlines (platform-dependent) | Byte-for-byte determinism across OSes |
| D19 | Unexpected internal exceptions (OverflowError, RecursionError) → one `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <text>` line, exit 1; recursion limit raised modestly (e.g. 10000) in the parser/analyzer/evaluator entry | Traceback | "Never a traceback" |
| D20 | Malformed dot-commands → `unknown command: <stripped line>` | Separate usage messages | Only template given |
| D21 | REPL with missing DIR → IOError line, exit 3 | Start REPL anyway | `connect` raises immediately |
| D22 | `ambiguous table file 'N'`: N as written in the query (for `schema()`, the argument as given) | File stem | Contract N rule |

## 6. Cost Estimates
Not applicable (no infrastructure; stdlib only).

## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)

Phase 1 — Foundations
- T1 Package skeleton, errors module, test scaffolding (`conftest.py`, fixtures emp/dept), stdlib-import guard test.
- T2 Lexer + tests.
- T3 Catalog/CSV loader + type inference + tests.

Phase 2 — Front end
- T4 AST nodes + parser + tests.
- T5 Analyzer (resolution, typing, aggregate/ORDER BY/DISTINCT validation, output names) + tests.

Phase 3 — Execution and API
- T6 Evaluate (value ops, LIKE) + executor (staged pipeline) + tests.
- T7 Formatting + library API (`connect`, `Connection`, `Result`, exports) + tests.

Phase 4 — Interfaces and acceptance
- T8 CLI one-shot + stream setup + exit codes + tests.
- T9 REPL + tests.
- T10 Acceptance suite AC1–AC11 verbatim + cross-cutting edge-case tests.

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Hidden tests check exact bytes, positions and messages | Single position helper; message constants; byte-mode subprocess tests (never `text=True`, which hides `\r\n` — Integration F32) |
| Python version drift (3.9 local vs ≥3.11 target): NUL in CSV (3.11), `sum()` float compensation (3.12), int↔str 4300-digit limit (3.11) | No `sum()` for floats; avoid NUL/huge-int tests; D1 compatibility rules |
| Windows newline/encoding differences | Reconfigure streams in `main()`; write `\n` explicitly; stdin `newline='\n'` |
| Python `bool` leaking into results | Comparisons return explicit `1`/`0` |
| Floor vs truncating integer division | Sign-aware `//` formula |
| Deep nesting → RecursionError | D19 guard |
| Regex LIKE pitfalls (DOTALL, `$`, backtracking) | Regex-free matcher |
| Case-insensitive test filesystems (macOS/Windows) | Skip `ambiguous table file` tests when two case-variant files cannot coexist |

## 9. Acceptance Criteria

All of `contract.md` AC1–AC12, verbatim, with fixtures `emp.csv` (`id,name,dept,salary` / `1,Ann,eng,100` / `2,Bob,eng,` / `3,Cid,ops,80` / `4,Dee,,80` / `5,Eve,ops,120`) and `dept.csv` (`code,title` / `eng,Engineering` / `ops,Operations` / `ops,Ops Dup` / `hr,Human Resources`):

- AC1 (R1, R19) `python -m minisql --data D "SELECT 1 AS one"` prints `one\n1\n`, exit 0; no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`.
- AC2 (R2, R21) `SELECT * FROM EMP` returns 5 rows; `--data missing` exits 3 with `IOError: data directory not found: missing`.
- AC3 (R3) `schema("emp")` is `[("id","INTEGER"),("name","TEXT"),("dept","TEXT"),("salary","INTEGER")]`.
- AC4 (R4, R21) `SELECT 1 # 2` → `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`.
- AC5 (R5) `SELECT 1 + 2 * 3, -2 * 3, NOT 1 = 2` → `1 + 2 * 3,-2 * 3,NOT 1 = 2` / `7,-6,1`.
- AC6 (R6) `select NAME from Emp e where E.Id = 1` → `name` / `Ann`.
- AC7 (R7) `SELECT name + 1 FROM emp` → `SemanticError at line 1, column 13: type mismatch: cannot apply '+' to TEXT and INTEGER`.
- AC8 (R8) `SELECT 7 / 2, -7 / 2, 7 % -2, 7.0 / 2, NULL / 0` → `3,-3,1,3.5,`.
- AC9 (R9) `SELECT name FROM emp WHERE dept NOT IN ('eng', NULL)` → header only.
- AC10 (R10) `SELECT salary * 2, name AS n FROM emp WHERE id = 1` → header `salary * 2,n`, row `200,Ann`.
- AC11 (R17) `connect(D).execute("SELECT AVG(salary) FROM emp")` has `types == ["REAL"]`, `rows == [(95.0,)]`.
- AC12 (R2–R21) All behaviour in the contract's Language reference, Interface contract and Error handling sections reproduced exactly; evidenced by the pytest suite covering §5 rules (each R1–R21 has at least one dedicated test).

Additional spec-level acceptance: `python -m pytest -q` passes from the repo root on the available interpreter; no traceback is producible by the CLI for any query in the test suite.

## 10. Dependencies on Prior Features
None.

## 11. Delegation to Future Specs
- Additional SQL features listed in Non-Goals.
- Performance work (hash joins, streaming execution) — the contract mandates nested-loop semantics and staged order, so any optimisation must preserve them exactly.
- NaN ordering/equality semantics (Python semantics used; not specified by the contract).

- **Codebase Analyst** (geeky-orchestration:code-explorer): repo state, module decomposition, 65 edge-case rules with contract quotes, ambiguity table A1–A29. Sources: `contract.md`, `brief.md`, `.gitignore`.

## 1. Executive Summary

Build `minisql`, a Python standard-library-only query engine that executes a read-only SQL subset over a directory of CSV files. Each `.csv` file is a table whose column types (INTEGER / REAL / TEXT) are inferred from the data. The engine is a real pipeline — tokenizer → recursive-descent parser producing an AST → semantic analyzer (name resolution, static typing, aggregate validation, table IO) → staged executor — exposed as a library API (`minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`), a one-shot CLI (`python -m minisql`) printing CSV or an aligned table, and an interactive REPL. Errors are always a single line naming the kind and exact query line/column; never a traceback. Output is byte-for-byte deterministic on Windows, macOS and Linux. Pytest tests accompany the implementation.

## 2. Problem Statement

### Current State
The repository contains only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore` (`__pycache__/`). There is no code, no tests, no prior spec (Codebase Analyst, repo scan).

### Impact of Inaction

## 3. Goals & Non-Goals

### Goals
- G1. Satisfy every functional requirement R1–R21 and acceptance criterion AC1–AC12 of `contract.md` exactly.
- G2. Engine structure: separate tokenizer, parser/AST, semantic analysis, executor modules.
- G3. Library API, one-shot CLI and REPL per contract interface rules.
- G4. Exact error classes, messages and positions; no traceback on any path.
- G5. Deterministic byte output on all three OSes (UTF-8, `\n`).
- G6. A pytest suite covering each requirement, all ACs verbatim, and the edge cases in §5.
- G7. Code runs on Python ≥ 3.11 (contract) and, for local verification in this environment, also on Python 3.9 (see D1).

### Non-Goals
- Writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL), subqueries, UNION, CASE, BETWEEN, scalar functions other than the five aggregates, RIGHT/FULL/CROSS joins, `COUNT(DISTINCT …)`, multiple statements per query.
- Indexes, query optimisation, caching of table data between `execute` calls (files are re-read on each `execute`).
- Any third-party runtime dependency; `sqlite3` or any SQL engine/parser (forbidden by R1).

## 4. Architecture

```
SQL text ─► lexer.tokenize ─► sqlparser.parse ─► analyzer.analyze(query, catalog) ─► executor.run(plan) ─► Result
                                                     │  (loads referenced CSVs, FROM order)
DIR ─► catalog.Catalog (scan dir, resolve stems, read/infer CSV)                    formatting.format_csv / format_table
api.connect / Connection ── cli.main (one-shot | repl.run)
```

## 5. Detailed Design

Each subsection restates the governing contract rule and adds the binding design decisions. Decision IDs (Dn) are collected in §5.12.

### 5.1 Errors and positions (R21)
- `MiniSQLError(Exception)` with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`. `str(err)` = `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO: `IOError: <message>`. Kind `Runtime` prints `RuntimeError at …` (class name `QueryRuntimeError`).
- All positions derive from an absolute code-point offset into the SQL text via one helper: `line = sql.count('\n', 0, off) + 1`; `column = off - (sql.rfind('\n', 0, off) + 1) + 1`. Lines split on `\n` only; tab and `\r` count as one column (Domain Expert F1).
- Message templates and positions exactly per the contract table (Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime/IO). `N`, `R`, `F` as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`); `OP` as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates.
- Phase order: lex the whole input → parse fully → semantic (including IO for referenced tables in FROM order) → execute. All static errors are raised before any row is evaluated.

### 5.2 Lexer (R4, R6)
- Whitespace exactly space, tab, `\r`, `\n`; anything else outside a token (e.g. NBSP, form feed, `#`, lone `!`) → `unexpected character 'X'` at that character.
- `--` comment to end of line (so `SELECT --1` is followed by EOF).
- Character classes are ASCII-only: identifiers `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; digits `[0-9]`. Never `str.isdigit/isalpha/isidentifier` or `\d` (Integration F25–26, Domain Expert F1).
- Keywords (case-insensitive, reserved): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`. Function names are identifiers.
- Quoted identifier `"..."` (`""` → `"`), may contain anything incl. newlines, may equal a keyword; unterminated → `unterminated quoted identifier` at the opening quote.
- String `'...'` (`''` → `'`), may span lines, backslash literal; unterminated → `unterminated string literal` at opening quote.
- Numbers: INTEGER `[0-9]+`; REAL `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. Longest match of these forms; if the next character is an ASCII letter, digit, `_` or `.` → `invalid number literal` at the literal start. Thus `12abc`, `1e`, `1e+`, `1..2`, `1.2.3`, `1_0`, `1.5e` are errors; `1.`, `1.e5`, `.5` are valid; `.` not followed by a digit is the `.` operator. REAL value = `float(text)`, INTEGER value = `int(text)`.
- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . ;` and `*`.
- Each token carries `kind`, `value`, `text = sql[start:end]`, `start`, `end`. An EOF token sits at offset `len(sql)` ("one past last input character").

### 5.3 Parser (R5)
- Recursive descent over the contract EBNF. Level 4 (comparison / IS / LIKE / IN) is non-associative: `cmp` parses at most one tail; a second comparison operator surfaces as `unexpected token '<text>'` at that operator (`a = b = c`, `a IS NULL IS NULL`).
- `NOT` binds looser than comparison (`NOT 1 = 2` = `NOT (1 = 2)` → 1); `1 = NOT 2` → ParseError at `NOT`.
- `unexpected token 'T'` uses the token's exact source text (strings keep their quotes, keywords keep written case). At EOF: `unexpected end of input` at offset `len(sql)`.
- Calls: `name "(" ("*" | expr) ")"`; whitespace allowed between name and `(`; quoted names may be calls. `COUNT()`, `COUNT(DISTINCT x)`, `f(a, b)`, `COUNT(t.*)` → ParseErrors at the offending token.
- `item`: `*` | `name . *` (3-token lookahead) | `expr [[AS] name]`; an alias without `AS` is any IDENT/QUOTED_IDENT token.
- `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take an INTEGER literal token only (`LIMIT -1`, `LIMIT 1.5` are ParseErrors); `OFFSET` without `LIMIT` is legal; `OFFSET … LIMIT …` is a ParseError at `LIMIT`. Optional single `;` then EOF.
- AST nodes record `start`/`end` (first to last character of the construct), a `pos` offset for error reporting (operator token for binary/unary/logical/comparison ops; the `LIKE`/`IN` keyword for `[NOT] LIKE`/`[NOT] IN` (D9); function-name token for calls; first token for column refs; the `*` token in calls; the ESCAPE string token), and a distinct `Paren(expr)` node whose span includes the parentheses (Domain Expert F1).

### 5.4 Data directory and CSV loading (R2, R3)
- `connect(DIR)`: if `DIR` is missing or not a directory → `DataIOError("data directory not found: DIR")` immediately (DIR as given, `str(os.fspath(DIR))`).
- Table discovery: fresh `os.scandir` on every `execute`/`tables()`; a table is an entry with `entry.is_file()` (follows symlinks; excludes directories, FIFOs, broken links) whose name ends with `.csv` case-insensitively; stem = `name[:-4]` (D12). Lookup is case-insensitive (`str.lower()`); two stems equal case-insensitively → `ambiguous table file '<name>'` (name as written in the query) for any reference.
- Read with `open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='')` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)`, streaming as the contract literally states (D5). Only tables referenced in FROM/JOIN are read, in FROM order, during semantic analysis.
- Records with zero fields (blank lines, before or after the header) are skipped. The first non-empty record is the header; no header → `<file>: empty file` (empty file, BOM-only, blank-lines-only).
- Header: names used verbatim; empty name → `<file>: empty column name`; duplicate names (case-insensitive) → `<file>: duplicate column 'C'` with `C` the second occurrence as written.
- Field-count mismatch → `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M` with N = `reader.line_num` after that record. `csv.Error` → `<file>: line N: malformed CSV` with N = `line_num` when raised. `UnicodeDecodeError` → `<file>: invalid UTF-8`. Other `OSError` while opening/reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` (D13; no contract template, defensive only).
- `<file>` is the base file name as on disk.
- Type inference per column over non-empty raw fields (no trimming) using `re.fullmatch` with explicit ASCII classes: all match `[+-]?[0-9]+` → INTEGER (`int`); else all match `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` → REAL (`float`); else TEXT (verbatim). No non-empty fields → TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. `re.fullmatch` is required (`re.match(...$)` would accept a trailing `\n`) (Codebase Analyst §3.35).
- `tables()` lists stems sorted by `(s.lower(), s)` without reading contents; ambiguous stems are both listed (D14). `schema(table)` loads the table (with IO errors as above) and returns `[(column, type)]` in header order; unknown table → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 (D15).

### 5.5 Name resolution and output names (R6, R10)
- Range name of a tableref = alias if present, else table name; a table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier (`emp.id` with `FROM emp e` → `unknown column 'emp.id'`). Duplicate range names (case-insensitive) → `duplicate table name 'N'` at the second tableref's range-name token.
- Unqualified `c` searches all FROM tables; `q.c` searches range `q`; zero matches → `unknown column 'R'`, more than one → `ambiguous column 'R'`, at the column-ref start. ON sees only tables introduced before or in its own join. Joins associate left. All name matching is case-insensitive.
- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in FROM order; `t.*` to that table's columns; unknown/hidden `t` → `unknown table 't'` at the `t` token (D10). `SELECT *` without FROM expands to zero columns (D11).
- Output name: alias as written (quotes removed, `""` → `"`); else for an unparenthesized column reference (qualified or not), the column's header name from the CSV; else verbatim source text `sql[item.start:item.end]` (keeps inner whitespace/comments/newlines; e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).

### 5.6 Static typing (R7)
- Types: INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, NULL (bare `NULL` literal only, plus results derived per rules below). LEFT JOIN does not change a column's static type (D2).
- Arithmetic `+ - * / %`: operands INTEGER/REAL/NULL else `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2` at the operator. Result REAL if either REAL; else NULL if both NULL; else INTEGER. Unary `-`/`+`: operand numeric/NULL else `cannot apply 'OP' to T`; result keeps operand type.
- Comparisons and each `IN` item vs `x`: both numeric, both TEXT, or either NULL; else two-type mismatch (OP as written; `IN` for IN). Result INTEGER.
- `LIKE`: both operands TEXT or NULL, else `cannot apply 'LIKE' to T1 and T2` at the `LIKE` token; `ESCAPE` string must be exactly one code point else `ESCAPE must be a single character` at the ESCAPE string. Result INTEGER.
- `IS [NOT] NULL`: any operand; INTEGER.
- `AND`/`OR`: operands numeric/NULL else two-type mismatch (`AND`/`OR`); `NOT`: single-type mismatch (`NOT`). Results INTEGER.
- `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` condition of type TEXT → `condition must be numeric, got TEXT` at the condition expression's start (first character, e.g. `(` for `WHERE (name)`). Checks run bottom-up, so inner operator mismatches are reported first.
- Aggregates: `COUNT(*)`/`COUNT(e)` → INTEGER (any type). `SUM`: INTEGER→INTEGER, REAL→REAL, NULL→NULL (D4), TEXT → `cannot apply 'SUM' to TEXT` at the function name. `AVG`: numeric/NULL → REAL, TEXT → `cannot apply 'AVG' to TEXT`. `MIN`/`MAX`: any type, keeps argument type. Non-COUNT `X(*)` → `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT` at the `*`. Unknown name → `unknown function 'F'` at the name (checked before the `*` rule, D16).
- Result `types` list uses `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"`, `"NULL"`.

### 5.7 Aggregation (R12)
- Aggregate query iff `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or ORDER BY.
- Structural identity via canonical keys after resolution: `Paren` transparent; column → `('col', table_idx, col_idx)`; literal → `('lit', TYPE, value)` (type tag so `1` ≠ `1.0`); operators by canonical op (`<>` ≡ `!=`, D8) and child keys; aggregates by upper-case name and `'*'`/argument key (Domain Expert F2).
- Validation (select, HAVING, ORDER BY): a node whose key matches a GROUP BY key is OK; an aggregate is OK (argument must contain no aggregate); a literal is OK; a bare column ref otherwise → `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate` at the column ref; else recurse. `*`/`t.*` → `'*' not allowed in aggregate query` at the `*`. Aggregates in WHERE, ON, GROUP BY or inside another aggregate → `aggregate function not allowed here` at that function name.
- GROUP BY has no ordinals or alias references (`GROUP BY 1` groups by the constant; HAVING cannot see aliases).
- Without GROUP BY: one group over the whole filtered input, even when empty; without HAVING exactly one row; HAVING filters to 0 or 1 row. With GROUP BY: empty input → zero rows; groups in first-seen order (dict keyed by tuple of key values; NULL equals NULL).
- `COUNT(*)` counts rows (including LEFT JOIN NULL-filled rows); `COUNT(e)` non-NULL values; all others ignore NULLs; over zero non-NULL values COUNT is 0, others NULL. SUM accumulates left-to-right with `+` (never `sum()`/`math.fsum`, whose float results differ across versions — Integration F23). AVG = sum/count with true division (exact int sum for INTEGER). MIN/MAX replace only on strict `<`/`>` (first seen kept on ties).

### 5.8 Execution and evaluation order (R8, R9, R11, R13–R16)
Staged full passes, exactly per contract:
1. FROM/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; every matching pair emitted; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled right side after all pairs for an unmatched left row. No FROM → exactly one empty row.
2. WHERE per row. 3. Group keys then aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. HAVING per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. ORDER BY keys. 7. DISTINCT (first occurrence kept; NULL equals NULL). 8. Stable sort. 9. OFFSET, then LIMIT.
- Consequences: `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp LIMIT 0` raises; `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp WHERE 0` does not; select errors are reported before ORDER BY key errors; no constant folding.
- Evaluator compiled to closures over flat joined-row tuples; column identity `(table_idx, col_idx)` maps to a flat index.
- `AND`: evaluate left; if false → 0 without right; else evaluate right; false → 0; else NULL if either NULL; else 1. `OR` mirror. NULL left still evaluates right. Truthiness: nonzero true, zero false (`0.0`, `-0.0` false), NULL unknown.
- Arithmetic: evaluate both operands left-to-right; NULL → NULL; zero divisor (INTEGER 0 or REAL ±0.0) for `/` or `%` → `division by zero` at the operator. INTEGER `/`: `q = abs(a)//abs(b)`, negated if signs differ; INTEGER `%`: `a - b*q` (sign of dividend). REAL (either operand REAL): `/` true division, `%` `math.fmod`, operands converted with `float()`. Never `int(a/b)` or Python `%` (Integration F21).
- Comparisons return `int` 1/0 (never `bool`), NULL if either operand NULL. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering; numerics compare numerically.
- `IN`: evaluate `x` then all items left-to-right (no short-circuit, D6); NULL if `x` NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item NULL; else 0; `NOT IN` negates with 3VL. `IS [NOT] NULL` → 1/0.
- `LIKE`: if any operand (value, pattern, escape) is NULL → NULL (checked first, D7). Otherwise compile the whole pattern: escape char `c` followed by `%`, `_`, or `c` → literal; followed by anything else or at end → `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. Match whole-string, case-sensitive, code-point-wise with a regex-free two-pointer wildcard matcher (`%` any sequence incl. empty, `_` exactly one code point incl. newline). `NOT LIKE` negates with 3VL. Never pre-validate at analysis time.
- ORDER BY resolution: bare INTEGER literal → 1-based ordinal after `*` expansion (`0` or > column count → `ORDER BY position N is out of range` at the ordinal, N = `str(int value)`); bare unqualified identifier equal (case-insensitive) to exactly one explicit select alias → that output column (two → `ambiguous column 'R'`); otherwise an expression over input rows (or groups). `-1`, `(1)` are expressions. With DISTINCT each item must be an ordinal, alias, or structurally identical to a select expression, else `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used` at the expression start; such items map to output-column values.
- Sort: successive stable `list.sort` passes from last key to first, key `(v is not None, v)`, `reverse=True` for DESC — NULL smallest (first ASC, last DESC); ties keep pre-sort order in both directions (Domain Expert F3).
- `LIMIT 0` → no rows; OFFSET past end → no rows.

### 5.9 Library API (R17)
```python
minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
Connection.tables() -> list[str]
Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
```
Exports: `connect`, `Connection`, `Result`, `format_csv`, `format_table`, `MiniSQLError`, `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`. Importing `minisql` must not alter `sys.stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None` (never `bool`).

### 5.10 Output formats (R18)
- Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
- CSV: header line, then one line per row; fields joined by `,`; every line ends `\n`. NULL → empty unquoted field. Quote a field (wrap in `"`, double inner `"`) iff it is the empty string, contains `,` `"` `\n` `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names use the same quoting. Hand-written (not `csv.writer`).
- Table: cell text = value text with `\n`→`\\n` and `\r`→`\\r` (two-character escapes), NULL → `NULL`; headers escaped the same way (D17). Width = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and NULL left-aligned (column alignment by the column's result type; NULL cells always left). Cells joined by ` | `; separator `-`×width joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; footer `(1 row)` or `(N rows)` (incl. `(0 rows)`); every line ends `\n`. A column of type NULL holds only NULL cells (left-aligned).

### 5.11 CLI and REPL (R19, R20)
- `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`; argparse with `allow_abbrev=False`, `--data` default `.`, `--format` `choices=['csv','table']` default `None` (one-shot → csv, REPL → table), positional `sql` `nargs='?'`; `args.sql is not None` → one-shot (so `""` is one-shot with empty SQL). Usage errors: argparse exit 2.
- Stream setup in `cli.main()` only (never at import): `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='backslashreplace', newline='\n')`; `sys.stdin` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', newline='\n')` (Integration F11–F15; D18).
- One-shot: `connect` first (missing DIR → `IOError: …` exit 3 before lexing); execute; format the full output string, then write once. Errors: stdout empty, stderr exactly `str(err) + "\n"`; exit 1 for Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime, 3 for IO, 0 on success.
- Top-level guard: catch `MiniSQLError`; catch `BrokenPipeError` (redirect stdout to devnull, exit 1); `KeyboardInterrupt` (exit 130); any other unexpected `Exception` (e.g. `OverflowError`, `RecursionError`) → a single line `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <exception text>` on stderr, exit 1 (D19) — never a traceback.
- REPL: prompt `minisql> ` when buffer empty, `   ...> ` (three spaces) otherwise, written to stdout without newline and flushed, regardless of TTY. Input not echoed. Read lines with `readline()`; strip one trailing `\n` only (keep `\r`; D18). With an empty buffer: a line whose stripped text (strip `' \t\r\n'`) starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise append the line (joined with `\n`); when the buffer right-stripped ends with `;`, execute it and clear the buffer.
- Commands (exact lower-case): `.help` (free text to stdout), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line; errors as one stderr line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit`, `.exit` (exit 0). Anything else (incl. `.format` with a bad/missing argument, `.schema` with no name) → stderr `unknown command: <stripped line>` (D20).
- Results print in the current format (CSV has no footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer. stdout is flushed before each stderr write.
- At EOF: a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. A missing `--data` DIR in REPL mode → `IOError: …` on stderr, exit 3 before the first prompt (D21).

Decisions taken where `contract.md` is silent or researchers diverged. Each picks the option closest to the contract text; the alternative is recorded.

| D10 | `q.*` with unknown/hidden `q` → `unknown table 'q'` at `q` | unknown column | Template list; table/name token |
| D11 | `SELECT *` without FROM → zero output columns, one row | SemanticError | Do not invent errors |
| D12 | Stem = `name[:-4]`; a file literally named `.csv` has stem `''` | `pathlib.Path.stem` | Contract "file stem" of `*.csv` |
| D13 | Non-decode OSError while reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` | Traceback | No-traceback rule; no template exists |
| D14 | `tables()` lists ambiguous stems (both) | Raise | "lists stems without reading file contents" |
| D15 | `schema(unknown)` → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 | DataIOError | Template exists only as Semantic |
| D16 | Unknown function reported before `'*'` argument rule | Reverse | Single-error oracle; name resolution precedes argument checks |
| D17 | Table format escapes `\n`/`\r` in header cells too | Escape only values | Preserves one-line rows |
| D18 | REPL stdin reconfigured to UTF-8 with `newline='\n'` (no CRLF translation; `\r` kept, lexer treats it as whitespace); stdin `errors='replace'` | Universal newlines (platform-dependent) | Byte-for-byte determinism across OSes |
| D19 | Unexpected internal exceptions (OverflowError, RecursionError) → one `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <text>` line, exit 1; recursion limit raised modestly (e.g. 10000) in the parser/analyzer/evaluator entry | Traceback | "Never a traceback" |
| D20 | Malformed dot-commands → `unknown command: <stripped line>` | Separate usage messages | Only template given |
| D21 | REPL with missing DIR → IOError line, exit 3 | Start REPL anyway | `connect` raises immediately |
| D22 | `ambiguous table file 'N'`: N as written in the query (for `schema()`, the argument as given) | File stem | Contract N rule |

## 6. Cost Estimates
Not applicable (no infrastructure; stdlib only).

## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)

Phase 1 — Foundations
- T1 Package skeleton, errors module, test scaffolding (`conftest.py`, fixtures emp/dept), stdlib-import guard test.
- T2 Lexer + tests.
- T3 Catalog/CSV loader + type inference + tests.

Phase 2 — Front end
- T4 AST nodes + parser + tests.
- T5 Analyzer (resolution, typing, aggregate/ORDER BY/DISTINCT validation, output names) + tests.

Phase 3 — Execution and API
- T6 Evaluate (value ops, LIKE) + executor (staged pipeline) + tests.
- T7 Formatting + library API (`connect`, `Connection`, `Result`, exports) + tests.

Phase 4 — Interfaces and acceptance
- T8 CLI one-shot + stream setup + exit codes + tests.
- T9 REPL + tests.
- T10 Acceptance suite AC1–AC11 verbatim + cross-cutting edge-case tests.

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Hidden tests check exact bytes, positions and messages | Single position helper; message constants; byte-mode subprocess tests (never `text=True`, which hides `\r\n` — Integration F32) |
| Python version drift (3.9 local vs ≥3.11 target): NUL in CSV (3.11), `sum()` float compensation (3.12), int↔str 4300-digit limit (3.11) | No `sum()` for floats; avoid NUL/huge-int tests; D1 compatibility rules |
| Windows newline/encoding differences | Reconfigure streams in `main()`; write `\n` explicitly; stdin `newline='\n'` |
| Python `bool` leaking into results | Comparisons return explicit `1`/`0` |
| Floor vs truncating integer division | Sign-aware `//` formula |
| Deep nesting → RecursionError | D19 guard |
| Regex LIKE pitfalls (DOTALL, `$`, backtracking) | Regex-free matcher |
| Case-insensitive test filesystems (macOS/Windows) | Skip `ambiguous table file` tests when two case-variant files cannot coexist |

## 9. Acceptance Criteria

All of `contract.md` AC1–AC12, verbatim, with fixtures `emp.csv` (`id,name,dept,salary` / `1,Ann,eng,100` / `2,Bob,eng,` / `3,Cid,ops,80` / `4,Dee,,80` / `5,Eve,ops,120`) and `dept.csv` (`code,title` / `eng,Engineering` / `ops,Operations` / `ops,Ops Dup` / `hr,Human Resources`):

- AC1 (R1, R19) `python -m minisql --data D "SELECT 1 AS one"` prints `one\n1\n`, exit 0; no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`.
- AC2 (R2, R21) `SELECT * FROM EMP` returns 5 rows; `--data missing` exits 3 with `IOError: data directory not found: missing`.
- AC3 (R3) `schema("emp")` is `[("id","INTEGER"),("name","TEXT"),("dept","TEXT"),("salary","INTEGER")]`.
- AC4 (R4, R21) `SELECT 1 # 2` → `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`.
- AC5 (R5) `SELECT 1 + 2 * 3, -2 * 3, NOT 1 = 2` → `1 + 2 * 3,-2 * 3,NOT 1 = 2` / `7,-6,1`.
- AC6 (R6) `select NAME from Emp e where E.Id = 1` → `name` / `Ann`.
- AC7 (R7) `SELECT name + 1 FROM emp` → `SemanticError at line 1, column 13: type mismatch: cannot apply '+' to TEXT and INTEGER`.
- AC8 (R8) `SELECT 7 / 2, -7 / 2, 7 % -2, 7.0 / 2, NULL / 0` → `3,-3,1,3.5,`.
- AC9 (R9) `SELECT name FROM emp WHERE dept NOT IN ('eng', NULL)` → header only.
- AC10 (R10) `SELECT salary * 2, name AS n FROM emp WHERE id = 1` → header `salary * 2,n`, row `200,Ann`.
- AC11 (R17) `connect(D).execute("SELECT AVG(salary) FROM emp")` has `types == ["REAL"]`, `rows == [(95.0,)]`.
- AC12 (R2–R21) All behaviour in the contract's Language reference, Interface contract and Error handling sections reproduced exactly; evidenced by the pytest suite covering §5 rules (each R1–R21 has at least one dedicated test).

Additional spec-level acceptance: `python -m pytest -q` passes from the repo root on the available interpreter; no traceback is producible by the CLI for any query in the test suite.

## 10. Dependencies on Prior Features
None.

## 11. Delegation to Future Specs
- Additional SQL features listed in Non-Goals.
- Performance work (hash joins, streaming execution) — the contract mandates nested-loop semantics and staged order, so any optimisation must preserve them exactly.
- NaN ordering/equality semantics (Python semantics used; not specified by the contract).

---

## Research basis and citations

- **Codebase Analyst** (geeky-orchestration:code-explorer): repo state, module decomposition, 65 edge-case rules with contract quotes, ambiguity table A1–A29. Sources: `contract.md`, `brief.md`, `.gitignore`.
- **Domain Expert** (engine architecture & SQL semantics): token/AST position model, Paren node, structural-identity keys, multi-pass stable sort, regex-free LIKE, 3VL/evaluation order, typing lattice. Sources: `contract.md`; https://docs.python.org/3/howto/sorting.html; https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html; local Python 3.9.6 experiments.
- **Integration Researcher** (Python stdlib & determinism): csv strict-mode error cases and `line_num`, UnicodeDecodeError surfacing, argparse exit codes, stream `reconfigure`, Windows newline behaviour, float `repr`, integer division, `sum()` 3.12 change, `os.scandir` semantics, byte-mode subprocess testing. Sources: https://docs.python.org/3/library/csv.html; https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html; https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html; https://docs.python.org/3/library/signal.html; https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html; https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.11.html; https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/71767; local 3.9.6 experiments.

**Assumptions:** hidden tests run on Python ≥ 3.11 with the same `csv` strict-mode behaviour for the default dialect as observed on 3.9.6 (no known 3.11–3.13 change other than NUL handling; unverified locally). Researcher disagreements resolved in D1 (interpreter availability) and D5 (CSV read model).
